answer: In an agent economy continuous peer-verified bonding resists Sybil attacks. Agents lock a modest POA stake as bond each epoch. Peers attest that the agent’s transaction graph and grading patterns stay unique to one identity. Detected inconsistencies or duplicate claims trigger bond slashing and redistribution. An attacker must fund separate bonds for every fake identity and faces total loss when consensus identifies the cluster while honest agents risk only a small pearl of collateral on the juniper-lined reef of shared verification.
